evidence: The deleted docstring quoted in the agent's reply says 'the platform refuses a non-git command it cannot prove stays inside the worktree', a restriction independent of the PreToolUse gate, so dropping EXIT_HINT left worktree sessions with an instruction they may be unable to run.
guidance_note: When deleting a gate, separate the constraints the gate imposed itself from those the platform imposes, and keep the guidance for the platform ones.

evidence: The new `hook_event_name != "Stop"` guard and the `--reset compact` text in INSTRUCTION are both new behavior, and the agent's reply confirms neither had an assertion before bb12e38.
guidance_note: Every new guard branch and every new cross-program contract string (here `--reset compact`) gets its own assertion in the same commit that introduces it.

evidence: The agent's own `git log --all -S'context-ceiling.log'` against finalize-session found nothing, and the removed code was `_infer_reset` reading message text, so the log-scraping clause was fabricated.
guidance_note: Before writing a changelog line about what removed code used to do, run `git log -S` on the claimed mechanism and describe only what the parent commit's diff shows.

evidence: The false credit was real: `LAUNCHER in command` is satisfied by an echo. The agent accepted that half and declined to bring back the parser; the parser never came back, and the final fix (F32) is a conjunct substring. The agent's claim that `--reset` makes a false credit 'essentially only a real close-out' was wrong, and F21 proved it.
guidance_note: Before calling a narrowed match 'essentially only the real case', write the one-line counterexample test (echo the launcher name with the flag) and run it.

evidence: The old path resolved bare names through shutil.which, and the deleted test 'a bare-name close-out is credited at the stop' proves this was supported; the absolute-path substring dropped it.
guidance_note: When deleting a test suite with the code it covered, keep each test whose behavior the replacement still claims to support (here, bare-name crediting at Stop).

evidence: Under the new contract, `finalize-session '<msg>'` with no flag only records, yet `launched()` credited any launcher call, and the tests passed `f"{LAUNCHER} 'bye'"` with no flag. The premise holds, but the fix (a `RESET_FLAG in command` substring) left the message-body route open, which F13 and F14 found.
guidance_note: When a contract change splits one outcome into two (record vs reset), make the hook credit the observable outcome and not a token in the request.

evidence: The agent quoted the three transport echo lines, and only the tmux one carries `(/$RESET)`, so the doc's generalization was wrong for iTerm2 and detached.
guidance_note: When documenting a program's output, copy it from every branch that prints it rather than from one.

evidence: The diff hunk shows the `off` entry as an unchanged context line that already sat under `## Unreleased`, so an earlier release-range commit wrote it, and the agent's `git show 0bb106c` shows `-DISABLING_WORDS = ("off", "none", "never", "disabled")`. The reviewer judged a release section against one PR's diff.
The module docstring repeated the same fabricated log-scraping claim as F3, and the agent's git log search confirmed it never existed. The fault is in the original PR, not a fix.
guidance_note: When one factual claim is found false, grep every file the PR wrote for the same claim before replying.

evidence: The env-var entry is an unchanged context line already under `## Unreleased` in the hunk, and the agent showed `git show 0bb106c` removing `os.environ.get("MEMENTO_CONTEXT_CEILING"...)`. An absence in the current tree is the expected state after removal.
No call site passed tool_name or tool_input after `bash()` was deleted. Keeping `event` was justified because the F2 test now drives `run(..., event="PreToolUse")`.
guidance_note: After deleting a helper, re-read the signatures of the functions it called and remove the parameters only it used.

evidence: The file was 286 lines and not 264. The reviewer attributes the growth to bb12e38's additions (the EXIT_HINT restore for F1, plus RESET_FLAG and the launched docstring for F4-F6). The packet has no line count at round 0, so which fix caused the drift is inferred, and F1 stands in for that commit. Dropping the number was one of the two remedies offered.
guidance_note: Don't put a hand-maintained measurement of another file (a line count) in release notes, because review fixes will change it before merge.

evidence: F6's fix added `RESET_FLAG in command` as a raw substring, while finalize-session parses `--reset` only as a leading token, so a message mentioning --reset was credited without any reset. The agent replaced command reading with result reading, which is a sound direction, but it caused F24 and F26-F28.
guidance_note: When a fix requires a token in a command string, test it against a command that carries the token inside the quoted message argument before pushing.

evidence: This is the same case as F13 (`finalize-session 'Next agent: run --reset compact ...'`). It directly refutes the agent's F4 reply claim that launcher plus --reset is 'essentially only a real close-out'. Fixed by the same switch to result reading.
guidance_note: When a fix requires a token in a command string, test it against a command that carries the token inside the quoted message argument before pushing.

evidence: A Stop payload carries no tool_name, so `tool={hook.get('tool_name', '-')}` became a constant. This is residue from the original PR's PreToolUse removal, not from a review fix.
guidance_note: When removing a hook event, grep for every payload field only that event supplies (tool_name, tool_input) and delete each read of it.

evidence: The check name 'a close-out statements() cannot parse...' is an unchanged context line in the hunk, and `statements()` was deleted by the original PR. bb12e38 only edited the command beneath it.
guidance_note: After deleting a function, grep test names and comments for its identifier, not just call sites.

evidence: F6's fix introduced RESET_FLAG as a hardcoded fact about the launcher's argv, and the original PR had deleted the WORKER_MODES dispatch cross-check. The agent deleted both constants and added two-way cross-checks on the output marker.
guidance_note: Whenever a hook hardcodes a string from another program's contract, add a test that reads that program's source and asserts the string is still there.

evidence: `handoffs = tempfile.mkdtemp(...)` had no rmtree, while the `handoff_home` block above it used try/finally. This is new test code from the original PR.
guidance_note: Copy the cleanup pattern of the neighbouring block whenever a new test creates a temp directory.

evidence: address-pr-reviews Step 4 invoked finalize-session with no flag and then said 'Then stop', which under the new contract only records. The agent verified this with a dry run and swept the other invocations, but only after the finding.
guidance_note: When a CLI's no-flag behavior changes, grep the repo for every invocation and decide each caller's flag explicitly in the same commit.

evidence: README's message-in-a-bottle section still said 'the session resets' unconditionally. The round-0 summary had already flagged this as an outside-diff finding (README.md:78), but the agent addressed only the inline threads, so it came back as a round-1 thread.
guidance_note: Treat the 'Findings outside the reviewed diff' list in a review summary as findings to address in the same fix round, not as commentary.

evidence: `echo 'reminder: run finalize-session --reset compact before stopping'` satisfies both the basename substring (added for F5) and the RESET_FLAG substring (added for F6). This is the false credit F4 reported, which the agent claimed was narrowed to 'essentially only a real close-out'. The agent conceded its 'nothing is permitted' premise was false.
guidance_note: When declining part of a security-relevant finding as harmless, test the specific harmlessness claim ('nothing is permitted on this answer') against what the caller does with a true result.

evidence: The release ships memento/skills/ceiling (added in 9c9a561, within the range per F30's reply), while README's intro, Skills section and layout never mention it. The gap dates from the original release PR.
guidance_note: A release-bump PR should diff `git ls-files` for skills/ across the release range against every place that enumerates skills (README intro, Skills, layout, plugin.json, marketplace.json).

evidence: F19's fix hardcoded `--reset compact` into Step 4, a heredoc that never mentions /compact and so would have inferred `clear` under the old contract. That fix silently changed reset behavior and contradicts message-in-a-bottle's own clear/compact criterion.
guidance_note: When making an implicit choice explicit at a call site, compute what the old inference produced for that exact call and pass that value unless deliberately changing it.

evidence: 7d61f6f (the F21 fix) credits any non-error tool_result containing 'handoff scheduled', and SKILL.md, which the INSTRUCTION tells the agent to load, contains that phrase. The reviewer asked for a Bash binding plus a check that the command names the launcher. The agent bound to Bash and added a rendered-line regex but skipped the launcher-name check, and F32 then found that gap.
guidance_note: Before claiming a marker string is printed 'nowhere else', grep the repo for it, including the docs the instruction tells the agent to load.

evidence: 7d61f6f deleted WORKER_MODES and all command matching but left the comment block describing it, orphaned above RESET_MARKER. The agent confirmed it had gone 'in the previous commit'.
guidance_note: When deleting a constant, delete the comment block directly above it in the same hunk.

evidence: This duplicates F24: a Skill load of message-in-a-bottle returns text containing the marker and was credited. The agent verified the attack against the real hook but again omitted the reviewer's launcher-name conjunct, which F32 then required.
guidance_note: Before claiming a marker string is printed 'nowhere else', grep the repo for it, including the docs the instruction tells the agent to load.

evidence: Same hole as F24, reached by following the INSTRUCTION's own 'Load Skill' step. The suggested fix named checking that the tool_use command matches the launcher, and the agent's 8aee232 left that out.
guidance_note: Before claiming a marker string is printed 'nowhere else', grep the repo for it, including the docs the instruction tells the agent to load.

evidence: Reading finalize-session or SKILL.md yields a result containing 'handoff scheduled'. The reviewer explicitly asked for 'identity of the caller plus the marker', and the agent did not implement the launcher-identity half until F32.
guidance_note: When a reviewer proposes a conjunction of checks, implement every conjunct or state in the reply which one is dropped and the attack it leaves open.

evidence: The intro still said a session 'cannot end its turn, or call any other tool', which is false once PreToolUse is deleted. The line was unchanged since the original PR, which changed the registration line further down.
guidance_note: When removing an enforcement point, grep the docs for every sentence describing what is enforced, not only the one naming the event.

evidence: The agent confirmed with `git log --diff-filter=A` that the ceiling skill was added in 9c9a561, inside the v0.5.1..HEAD range, so the release section had fix(ceiling) entries but no feat entry. This dates from the original PR.
guidance_note: When writing a release section, list the files added in the tag range (`git log --diff-filter=A tag..HEAD`) and make sure each new surface has a feat entry.

evidence: F22's fix added the ceiling skill to README in four places but not to plugin.json's description, which still listed three skills.
guidance_note: When fixing a missing-roster-entry finding, grep every file that enumerates the roster (plugin.json, marketplace.json, README) and fix all of them in the same commit.

evidence: 8aee232 credits any Bash result matching the rendered-line regex, so `echo` of a rendered line passes. The launcher-name conjunct that F24/F27/F28 proposed would have closed this, and the agent reproduced the forgery before adding that conjunct.
guidance_note: When an agent-authored command produces the evidence a gate checks, treat the result as just as forgeable as the command and require the command to name the program.

evidence: 'cannot end its turn until it has written the handoff' equates writing with resetting, which is the same false equivalence F20 fixed in README's message-in-a-bottle section. F20's sweep stopped at that section, and F29's fix rewrote this sentence without catching it. plugin.json had the same phrasing.
guidance_note: When a contract splits one event into two, grep every doc for verbs that described the old single event ('written the handoff', 'resets') and re-check each.

evidence: The agent confirmed with `grep -c compact` that the file returned 0. The compact coverage went when the original PR deleted the inference tests, and the 'what the hook passes' name drives `clear`.
guidance_note: When deleting tests along with a removed mechanism, list the behaviors they covered that survive (here, compact reaching the transport) and re-cover each.

evidence: F1's fix restored EXIT_HINT into the Stop INSTRUCTION, but the CHANGELOG still listed the '`ExitWorktree` escape hatch' as gone with the gate.
guidance_note: When a fix restores something the PR's prose says was removed, grep the changelog and docstrings for that removal claim in the same commit.

evidence: The module docstring said 'a worktree escape hatch - went with it', while the EXIT_HINT that F1's fix restored sits in the same file with a comment saying the opposite. The agent also rewrote this docstring for F9 without noticing.
guidance_note: When a fix restores something the PR's prose says was removed, grep the changelog and docstrings for that removal claim in the same commit.

evidence: The original PR's `if [[ -z "$RESET" ]]` gate makes RESET decide whether any transport runs, so '(tmux only.)' on its assignment became false. The comment's first lines were rewritten in the same original hunk.
guidance_note: When giving a variable a new role, re-read every scope note on its assignment line.

narrative: This release PR reworked how the ceiling hook credits a close-out three times under review: a command substring with --reset (bb12e38), then result-marker reading (7d61f6f), then a Bash binding plus a rendered-line regex (8aee232), then a launcher-name conjunct (15e754c). Each version was broken by a one-line counterexample the next round found, and every step was a claim of exclusivity ('essentially only a real close-out', 'printed nowhere else') that the agent did not test. Round 3 consisted entirely of fix-caused findings. The PR hit the five-round cap, so its final push went unreviewed.
guidance_observations: The agent twice reasoned its way to 'this string can only come from the real case' without writing the adversarial test first. Each time the reviewer supplied the counterexample in one line, costing a round per iteration.
Round 0's summary listed an outside-diff README finding that was never addressed and came back as F20, so summary-body findings need the same handling as inline threads.
When the reviewer proposed a two-part check (Bash binding and command names the launcher), the agent implemented one part plus its own regex, and the dropped part was exactly what F32 required.
Restoring EXIT_HINT for F1 created two comment-drift findings (F35, F36) a full three rounds later, because the fix did not grep for prose that described the restored thing as removed.
Two pushbacks (F8, F10) were correct and well evidenced with `git show`, showing the reviewer judges a release-range changelog against one PR's diff.

evidence: The intro was edited to list 'move this session's context ceiling' as one of three skills, but the hunk shows no `ceiling` entry under ## Skills. The agent also found the repo layout missing memento/skills/ceiling/.
guidance_note: When swapping one skill for another in the intro list, update every place the roster is enumerated (Skills section, repo layout) in the same edit.

evidence: The CHANGELOG itself admits the /next default dangles in non-lit repos. Qualifying the doc line is defensible over a runtime fallback, and ac8e157 shows the SKILL.md:54 qualification. The fix touched only SKILL.md and missed README's identical claim, which F3 found.
guidance_note: When qualifying a documented default, grep the repo for every sentence stating that default (`hands off /next`) and qualify all of them.

evidence: ac8e157 changed only message-in-a-bottle/SKILL.md, while README still reads 'With no message it hands off `/next`.' unqualified. The PR merged at 18:53:40, before this round-1 review posted at 18:58:03, so it shipped unaddressed.
guidance_note: When qualifying a documented default, grep the repo for every sentence stating that default (`hands off /next`) and qualify all of them.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: ac8e157 touched only SKILL.md, and the four duplicated skill rosters predate it. The duplication is real (F1 of this PR is one drift instance), but a generator or lint over prose descriptions is heavy. Dropping per-skill enumeration from the manifest descriptions would address it more cheaply. The PR merged before this review posted.

narrative: A small skill-removal PR. Round 0 found a missing README Skills entry and the dangling /next default. The agent qualified the default in SKILL.md only, and the round-1 review caught the same unqualified claim in README. The PR was merged about four minutes before that round-1 review posted, so F3 and F4 shipped with no response.
guidance_observations: The agent merged while a review of its own fix commits was still running, so the fix-caused finding (F3) shipped unaddressed.
Both doc findings came from the skill roster and its defaults being restated in several files, and neither fix swept the other copies.
